sources.title: Outpatient treatment of COVID-19 and incidence of post-COVID-19 condition over 10 months (COVID-OUT): a multicentre, randomised, quadruple-blind, parallel-group, phase 3 trial
sources.population: Adults 30–85, overweight or obesity, acute COVID symptoms under 7 days; no known prior infection
sources.preview: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of later clinician-diagnosed Long COVID after metformin began during acute infection, but this result remains provisional while an indexed correction is reconciled. The result does not establish treatment benefit for people who already have Long COVID. The long-term analysis used a selected follow-up group. Cumulative-incidence percentages are withheld because the acquired source reports conflicting control values.

locators.table_figure: Figure 2 and Results paragraph beginning cumulative incidence

sources.correction: The journal issued a correction (PMID 37666258). Conflicting cumulative-incidence values make the absolute risk reduction uncertain.
sources.intervention: Oral immediate-release metformin; titrated over 6 days to 1500 mg/day, continued through day 14
sources.decisiveLimit: The long-term follow-up population was selected from an acute-infection trial. An indexed correction and conflicting cumulative-incidence values limit interpretation of the absolute effect.

sources.title: Metformin on the Presence of COVID-19 Symptoms 6 Months after Infection: The ACTIV-6 Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Accelerating COVID-19 Therapeutic Interventions and Vaccines (ACTIV)-6 Study Group and Investigators
sources.design: Quadruple-blind randomized decentralized placebo-controlled platform trial
sources.population: Outpatients at least 30 years old with acute COVID; prior infection/vaccination allowed
sources.preview: This randomized prevention trial did not meet its efficacy threshold for symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months. The secondary clinician-diagnosis point estimate favored metformin, but its interval included no difference and does not replace the primary result. The study had few observed events and missing follow-up responses. These findings concern treatment during acute infection, not starting metformin to treat an established Long COVID illness.

Table 3 secondary clinician diagnosis; Table 2 raw counts

sources.decisiveLimit: Few long-term events, 593 missing symptom outcomes and a secondary diagnosis endpoint limit precision and interpretation.

sources.title: Nirmatrelvir-Ritonavir and Symptoms in Adults With Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection: The STOP-PASC Randomized Clinical Trial
sources.population: Adults with at least two moderate/severe core PASC symptoms, at least 3 months duration
sources.preview: A 15-day nirmatrelvir–ritonavir course did not significantly improve the selected symptom outcomes in STOP-PASC. Participants already had long COVID, so the question differed from acute treatment or prevention. Symptoms improved in both groups. The small, selected, single-center population limits broader conclusions, and later trials still require full-text reconciliation. The source includes a correction to Figure 2.

sources.decisiveLimit: July 22 2024 correction repositions dashed lines in Figure 2. Current PMC article explicitly includes correction.

guides.title: Metformin and long COVID prevention
guides.description: What the metformin trials found about later Long COVID after treatment during acute infection.

sections.label: Answer
sections.title: What did the prevention trials find?
sections.paragraph: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of later clinician-diagnosed Long COVID, although an indexed correction and conflicting cumulative-incidence values complicate interpretation. ACTIV-6 did not meet its efficacy threshold for its primary long-term symptom outcome.

sentences.text: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of later clinician-diagnosed Long COVID, although an indexed correction and conflicting cumulative-incidence values complicate interpretation. ACTIV-6 did not meet its efficacy threshold for its primary long-term symptom outcome.

sections.label: Context
sections.title: When treatment began
sections.paragraph: Both studies began treatment during acute COVID-19. They address prevention of later illness; the separate Korean trial tested treatment after Long COVID symptoms were already established.

sentences.text: Both studies began treatment during acute COVID-19. They address prevention of later illness; the separate Korean trial tested treatment after Long COVID symptoms were already established.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.title: Symptoms and diagnosis were different outcomes
sections.paragraph: In ACTIV-6, the adjusted risk difference for symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months was −0.8 percentage points, with a 95% credible interval of −2.2 to 0.6. The secondary clinician-diagnosis estimate was −0.7 percentage points, with an interval of −1.5 to 0.1. Both intervals included no difference.

sentences.text: In ACTIV-6, the adjusted risk difference for symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months was −0.8 percentage points, with a 95% credible interval of −2.2 to 0.6. The secondary clinician-diagnosis estimate was −0.7 percentage points, with an interval of −1.5 to 0.1. Both intervals included no difference.

sections.label: Limits
sections.title: Why the findings differ
sections.paragraph: COVID-OUT enrolled adults with overweight or obesity and no known prior infection. ACTIV-6 included a different vaccination and prior-infection context, had relatively few long-term events and 593 missing symptom outcomes. These differences limit direct comparison.

sentences.text: COVID-OUT enrolled adults with overweight or obesity and no known prior infection. ACTIV-6 included a different vaccination and prior-infection context, had relatively few long-term events and 593 missing symptom outcomes. These differences limit direct comparison.

faqs.question: Does a diagnosis endpoint measure every persistent symptom?
faqs.answer: No. A clinician diagnosis and a symptom-based endpoint count different outcomes, as illustrated by ACTIV-6’s primary and secondary analyses.

sentences.text: No. A clinician diagnosis and a symptom-based endpoint count different outcomes, as illustrated by ACTIV-6’s primary and secondary analyses.

guides.title: Metformin for established long COVID
guides.description: The randomized metformin result for recovery after Long COVID was already established.

sections.label: Answer
sections.title: Did metformin improve recovery?
sections.paragraph: The South Korean randomized trial found no significant improvement in eight-week recovery after a two-week metformin course. Recovery occurred in 84 of 132 metformin participants and 90 of 132 placebo participants.

sentences.text: The South Korean randomized trial found no significant improvement in eight-week recovery after a two-week metformin course. Recovery occurred in 84 of 132 metformin participants and 90 of 132 placebo participants.

sections.label: Context
sections.title: What recovery meant
sections.paragraph: The trial defined recovery using its PASC symptom-index threshold. That endpoint measures the trial’s specified recovery criterion; it does not imply that every symptom had disappeared.

sentences.text: The trial defined recovery using its PASC symptom-index threshold. That endpoint measures the trial’s specified recovery criterion; it does not imply that every symptom had disappeared.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.title: What the comparison establishes
sections.paragraph: Both groups improved, but metformin did not show an advantage over placebo. The result concerns the tested two-week course and population, including the trial’s limitation in applying the findings to more severe or persistent illness.

sentences.text: Both groups improved, but metformin did not show an advantage over placebo. The result concerns the tested two-week course and population, including the trial’s limitation in applying the findings to more severe or persistent illness.

sections.label: Limits
sections.title: The separate fatigue report was retracted
sections.paragraph: The original REVIVE fluvoxamine and metformin report has a notice of retraction and republication. Its original fatigue findings are excluded from benefit conclusions.

sentences.text: The original REVIVE fluvoxamine and metformin report has a notice of retraction and republication. Its original fatigue findings are excluded from benefit conclusions.

faqs.question: Does this trial settle every treatment duration?
faqs.answer: No. It tested a two-week course with recovery measured at eight weeks. Longer courses and different illness populations are different research questions.

sentences.text: No. It tested a two-week course with recovery measured at eight weeks. Longer courses and different illness populations are different research questions.

guides.title: Nirmatrelvir–ritonavir for long COVID
guides.description: What randomized trials of extended nirmatrelvir–ritonavir found in established Long COVID.

sections.label: Answer
sections.title: What did the trials find?
sections.paragraph: STOP-PASC did not demonstrate a significant improvement in its primary symptom-severity outcome. RECOVER-VITAL also reported no significant primary benefit in its studied symptom groups.

sentences.text: STOP-PASC did not demonstrate a significant improvement in its primary symptom-severity outcome. RECOVER-VITAL also reported no significant primary benefit in its studied symptom groups.

guides.title: Metformin
guides.description: How metformin works, its investigated benefits across infections, cancer, neurological conditions and physical function, and its safety.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: What is metformin?
sections.paragraph: Metformin is an oral glucose-lowering medicine in the biguanide class. In the United States, immediate-release metformin tablets are approved alongside diet and exercise for type 2 diabetes in adults and children aged 10 years and older. It reduces the liver’s glucose production and improves the body’s response to insulin; those established uses are distinct from the repurposing investigations discussed here. Researchers are studying whether its effects on metabolism, cellular energy sensing and inflammatory pathways can help in acute COVID-19 and Long COVID, Parkinson’s disease, cognition in schizophrenia, and age-related loss of muscle function. Cancer research includes trials in prostate, lung, breast and pancreatic cancer, studies of recurrent colorectal adenomas after polyp removal, and laboratory work in multiple myeloma. The findings vary by condition and outcome: promising biological effects have often failed to translate into clinical benefit, and preventing a condition, treating established disease and changing a laboratory marker are different questions.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: The benefits being investigated include reducing Long COVID risk, improving cognition in schizophrenia, preserving physical function in older adults and improving Parkinson’s symptoms. A small schizophrenia trial reported improved cognitive-test scores with metformin, while the Parkinson’s pilot and the MET-PREVENT sarcopenia trial did not demonstrate improvements in their main clinical outcomes. For Long COVID, COVID-OUT reported a prevention signal, although a correction notice and inconsistent control percentages complicate interpretation; ACTIV-6 did not meet its primary efficacy threshold, and a separate trial found no improved recovery after symptoms were established. Cancer trials have generally not demonstrated the hoped-for treatment benefits; a separate colorectal study found fewer recurrent adenomas after polyp removal, which is a prevention outcome.

questions.question: Does metformin improve symptoms of Parkinson’s disease?
questions.answer: A three-month pilot randomized 60 people to metformin or placebo alongside levodopa/carbidopa. Clinical scores improved within the metformin group, but the comparison between groups did not show a statistically significant benefit on the total Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale. The trial was small, used a per-protocol analysis and was too short to establish whether metformin slows disease progression.

questions.question: What has the schizophrenia research found about cognition?
questions.answer: In a 72-person open-label randomized trial, adding metformin to antipsychotic treatment improved the composite cognitive-test score by an estimated 3.43 points more than antipsychotics alone after 24 weeks (95% CI 1.83–5.02). The participants were predominantly young adults, 59 completed follow-up, and the study lacked a placebo group; larger blinded studies are needed to confirm the size and practical importance of this effect. A later analysis of the same trial linked changes in metabolites and hippocampal connectivity with cognitive changes.

questions.question: Does metformin improve muscle strength or physical function?
questions.answer: The 2025 MET-PREVENT trial randomized 72 older adults with probable sarcopenia and prefrailty or frailty to metformin or placebo for four months. It found no walking-speed benefit: the adjusted difference was 0.001 m/s (95% CI −0.06 to 0.06), and metformin was poorly tolerated in this population. The 2023 review described inconsistent results: some research suggested faster walking, but strength outcomes were not consistently improved and exercise adaptations could be reduced. In the MASTERS trial, adding metformin to resistance training reduced muscle growth in healthy older adults; the difference in strength gains was not statistically significant.

questions.question: Does taking metformin during COVID-19 prevent Long COVID?
questions.answer: COVID-OUT reported fewer later clinician-diagnosed cases when treatment began during acute infection, but the estimate remains provisional because the report contains inconsistent control percentages and has a published correction. ACTIV-6 examined symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months and did not meet its prespecified threshold for benefit. The trials enrolled different populations and used different outcomes, leaving uncertainty about how much prevention benefit metformin provides.

questions.question: Does metformin help when Long COVID is already established?
questions.answer: A randomized South Korean trial did not find improved recovery after a two-week course of metformin in people with persistent symptoms. That result concerns the population and short treatment course tested; it does not establish the effect of longer courses or treatment in every Long COVID subgroup. A separate metformin-and-fluvoxamine fatigue report was retracted and republished; its original findings cannot serve as reliable evidence of metformin benefit.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Metformin commonly causes diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal discomfort; longer use can lower vitamin B12. Its major serious risk is lactic acidosis, particularly with impaired kidney function, hypoxia, liver disease or excessive alcohol intake.

sections.label: Dosing
sections.title: What schedules have repurposing trials tested?
sections.paragraph: The COVID-OUT and ACTIV-6 prevention trials tested a 14-day course of immediate-release metformin, increasing to 1,500 mg daily. The Parkinson’s pilot used 500 mg twice daily for three months, while the schizophrenia trial used up to 1,500 mg daily for 24 weeks. These studies tested different treatment schedules for different conditions; they did not establish one repurposing dose or demonstrate equivalent outcomes with extended-release metformin.

Release formulation also matters: the Long COVID prevention trials described here used immediate-release metformin and did not compare it with an extended-release product.

sections.paragraph: The U.S. prescribing information lists metformin as an adjunct to diet and exercise for type 2 diabetes in adults and children aged 10 years and older. sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The human evidence spans prevention, treatment and physical or cognitive function, with different populations, comparators and follow-up periods. Several cancer trials did not demonstrate the expected clinical benefit; adenoma recurrence after polyp removal is a separate prevention outcome. The schizophrenia metabolite and imaging report analyzes the same trial as the earlier cognitive report, so it does not add a second independent trial. Cell and mouse findings explain biological rationale but cannot establish patient benefit. COVID-OUT has a published correction notice and conflicting control-group percentages in the available report. Its long-term diagnosis estimate should be read with that qualification. The original REVIVE fatigue report has a notice of retraction and republication; its original results are not used as evidence of benefit.

Repurposing studies ask two different questions: whether treatment during acute infection reduces later illness, and whether treatment helps people who already have persistent symptoms.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: A source beside every claim
sections.paragraph: Use this guide to turn a drug-repurposing headline into a precise reading question before a conversation with a qualified professional. Write down the condition and its stage, the people of interest, the exact intervention, the comparison, the outcome, and the follow-up period. Then keep the original source beside your notes and make the unresolved points visible. The printable worksheet provides room for that work; completing it does not establish that a medicine is appropriate for you.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.title: Find out what you actually read
sections.paragraph: An abstract gives a short account of a report, while the main paper contains separate methods, results, discussion, and reference sections. Basic research, clinical trials, and reviews serve different purposes; a review brings together other studies rather than becoming another original trial. In the United States, off-label use can involve a different condition, route, or dose; approval for one use does not establish approval for every proposed use. Record the source type, the sections you could read, and the jurisdiction of any official status check.

sections.label: Decisions
sections.title: Compare the question with the study
sections.paragraph: A controlled trial compares an experimental group with a control group, which may receive usual care or an inactive intervention. Knowledge of which treatment was received can influence participants’ or investigators’ impressions of improvement. guides.title: Valproic acid
guides.description: An antiseizure medicine studied as an epigenetic modifier in cancer, with important toxicity findings.

sentences.text: Valproate’s oncology rationale is epigenetic, distinct from seizure control. Its combination trials make tolerability central to interpreting any response signal.

sentences.text: Valproate did not improve remission or survival in a randomized older-adult AML trial. A small head and neck combination trial stopped for toxicity; breast research showed histone acetylation.

questions.question: What happened in the head and neck trial?
questions.answer: Enrollment stopped after ten patients; nine were evaluable and the response rate was 88%, but the uncontrolled design and severe toxicity limit the benefit interpretation.

sentences.text: Enrollment stopped after ten patients; nine were evaluable and the response rate was 88%, but the uncontrolled design and severe toxicity limit the benefit interpretation.

questions.question: Did valproate improve AML remission with decitabine?

sentences.text: No. Remission was 17.8% with valproate versus 17.2% without it; odds ratio 1.06 (95% CI 0.51–2.21). No survival difference was observed.

sections.label: Contraindications

sections.label: Interactions

sentences.text: Carbapenem antibiotics can sharply lower valproate levels and compromise seizure control. Aspirin can increase the unbound fraction; other sedatives add central effects.

sections.label: Results

sections.label: Status

sections.label: Evidence

sections.label: Connections

sentences.text: Head and neck and breast cancer research asks about treatment sensitization; AML research emphasizes differentiation of immature blood cells.

sentences.text: Any useful oncology regimen must improve disease outcomes while avoiding additive marrow, hepatic, and other toxicity from combined therapy.

guides.title: Acute COVID-19
guides.description: Repurposed medicines in acute COVID-19: antiviral treatment, inflammatory pathways and randomized results.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Acute COVID-19 is the illness caused by a current SARS-CoV-2 infection. Its course ranges from mild respiratory symptoms to severe illness, with older age and certain medical conditions increasing risk. Drug studies have tested ways to reduce viral replication or the harmful host response before illness progresses.

sentences.text: Acute COVID-19 is the illness caused by a current SARS-CoV-2 infection. Its course ranges from mild respiratory symptoms to severe illness, with older age and certain medical conditions increasing risk.
Drug studies have tested ways to reduce viral replication or the harmful host response before illness progresses.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: The COVID-OUT trial tested metformin, ivermectin and fluvoxamine in adults with overweight or obesity. None significantly reduced its primary composite of hypoxaemia, emergency care, hospitalization or death. Nirmatrelvir with ritonavir has a separate established role in early treatment of eligible people at higher risk of severe COVID-19.

sentences.text: The COVID-OUT trial tested metformin, ivermectin and fluvoxamine in adults with overweight or obesity. None significantly reduced its primary composite of hypoxaemia, emergency care, hospitalization or death.

questions.question: Is an acute COVID-19 result also a Long COVID result?
questions.answer: No. The acute COVID-OUT report measured progression during the infection; the later follow-up asked about clinician-diagnosed Long COVID. Different follow-up periods and endpoints can give different answers.

sentences.text: No. The acute COVID-OUT report measured progression during the infection; the later follow-up asked about clinician-diagnosed Long COVID. Different follow-up periods and endpoints can give different answers.

sections.label: Safety

sections.label: Comparisons

sentences.text: Hospitalization prevention in a high-risk group cannot be equated with shortening mild symptoms in a lower-risk group. The COVID-OUT trial and outpatient antiviral recommendations concern different drugs, eligibility criteria and outcomes.

sections.label: Evidence

sections.label: Connections

sentences.text: The Long COVID page follows the prevention and persistent-symptom questions beyond the acute infection.

faqs.answer: Outpatient antiviral treatment is started early, within a short interval after symptom onset, because it targets viral replication during the acute illness.

guides.title: Epithelial ovarian or fallopian-tube carcinoma
guides.description: Epithelial ovarian and fallopian-tube cancers, and the evidence behind itraconazole combinations.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube and primary peritoneal cancers arise in closely related tissues and are treated using overlapping approaches. Histological subtype, stage and prior response to platinum chemotherapy influence the treatment question. Repurposing research includes itraconazole in recurrent ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a specific subtype that can respond poorly to cytotoxic treatment.

sentences.text: Epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube and primary peritoneal cancers arise in closely related tissues and are treated using overlapping approaches. Histological subtype, stage and prior response to platinum chemotherapy influence the treatment question.
Repurposing research includes itraconazole in recurrent ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a specific subtype that can respond poorly to cytotoxic treatment.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: A retrospective series combined itraconazole with chemotherapy in nine patients with recurrent or persistent clear cell carcinoma. Responses were observed, but all patients received combination treatment and there was no randomized chemotherapy-only group. The fenbendazole profile covers its separate ovarian-cancer research.

sentences.text: A retrospective series combined itraconazole with chemotherapy in nine patients with recurrent or persistent clear cell carcinoma. Responses were observed, but all patients received combination treatment and there was no randomized chemotherapy-only group.
The fenbendazole profile covers its separate ovarian-cancer research.

questions.question: Did itraconazole itself produce the tumor responses?
questions.answer: The series cannot separate itraconazole’s contribution from chemotherapy, patient selection or other care. Its findings support a combination-treatment hypothesis rather than a measured advantage attributable to itraconazole alone.

sentences.text: The series cannot separate itraconazole’s contribution from chemotherapy, patient selection or other care. Its findings support a combination-treatment hypothesis rather than a measured advantage attributable to itraconazole alone.

sections.label: Safety

sentences.text: The study added itraconazole to cytotoxic chemotherapy, so both the chemotherapy regimen and combination tolerability matter. Its small size cannot characterize uncommon toxicity.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy form part of established care described by NCI. The itraconazole series did not test replacement of those treatments or compare itraconazole with modern biomarker-directed maintenance therapy.

sentences.text: Surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy form part of established care described by NCI. The itraconazole series did not test replacement of those treatments or compare itraconazole with modern biomarker-directed maintenance therapy.

sections.label: Evidence

sections.label: Connections

sentences.text: Itraconazole has also been studied in prostate, lung and basal cell cancers, using different combinations and endpoints.

faqs.question: Why are ovarian and fallopian-tube cancers discussed together?
faqs.answer: These epithelial cancers have related biological origins and overlapping staging and treatment approaches. Histology and molecular features still matter within that shared category.

guides.title: Glioblastoma
guides.description: Why glioblastoma researchers are testing existing drugs, including mebendazole, alongside standard treatment.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Glioblastoma is an aggressive glioma that infiltrates brain tissue. Treatment commonly combines surgery where feasible with radiation and chemotherapy, but infiltration makes complete removal difficult. Mebendazole, an antiparasitic medicine, has been investigated as an addition to temozolomide in newly diagnosed high-grade gliomas.

guides.description: Low-dose naltrexone in fibromyalgia: the pain-processing rationale and the results of a larger placebo-controlled trial.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Fibromyalgia causes widespread pain and tenderness, often with fatigue, unrefreshing sleep and difficulty thinking clearly. Research points to altered pain processing rather than a single damaged joint or muscle. Low-dose naltrexone has been studied as a way to change central pain modulation.

sentences.text: Fibromyalgia causes widespread pain and tenderness, often with fatigue, unrefreshing sleep and difficulty thinking clearly. Research points to altered pain processing rather than a single damaged joint or muscle.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: In a 2024 trial of 99 women, naltrexone did not produce superior pain relief over placebo after 12 weeks. The between-group pain difference was −0.34 points on an 11-point scale, with a 95% confidence interval from −0.95 to 0.27.

sentences.text: In a 2024 trial of 99 women, naltrexone did not produce superior pain relief over placebo after 12 weeks. The between-group pain difference was −0.34 points on an 11-point scale, with a 95% confidence interval from −0.95 to 0.27.

sentences.text: It did not demonstrate the primary pain benefit. Exploratory findings concerning memory or pain modulation address different outcomes and need confirmation rather than being substituted for the pain result.

guides.description: Low-dose naltrexone and ME/CFS: what immune-cell experiments can explain and what they do not measure.

sections.paragraph: ME/CFS is a disabling multisystem illness marked by reduced ability to carry out usual activities, unrefreshing sleep and post-exertional malaise. sentences.text: ME/CFS is a disabling multisystem illness marked by reduced ability to carry out usual activities, unrefreshing sleep and post-exertional malaise. Physical or mental effort can cause a delayed worsening of symptoms.

sections.label: Options

sections.paragraph: Compulsive sexual behavior disorder involves persistent difficulty controlling repetitive sexual behavior that causes marked distress or impairment. guides.title: Treatment-resistant depression
guides.description: Pramipexole augmentation for treatment-resistant depression, including the dopamine rationale and randomized trial evidence.

sections.paragraph: Treatment-resistant depression describes continuing depressive illness despite adequate treatment attempts. sentences.text: Treatment-resistant depression describes continuing depressive illness despite adequate treatment attempts. Its symptoms can include loss of pleasure, motivation and daily function as well as persistent low mood.

sections.paragraph: Randomization assigned itraconazole doses; the study was explicitly noncomparative. With 29 men at the higher dose and 17 at the lower dose, estimates are imprecise.

sentences.text: Randomization assigned itraconazole doses; the study was explicitly noncomparative. With 29 men at the higher dose and 17 at the lower dose, estimates are imprecise.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The basal cell carcinoma page examines Hedgehog signaling in another itraconazole study, with different tumor biology and outcomes.

sentences.text: The basal cell carcinoma page examines Hedgehog signaling in another itraconazole study, with different tumor biology and outcomes.

faqs.question: What is the prostate?
faqs.answer: It is a gland in the male reproductive system that contributes fluid to semen. A prostate cancer study’s stage and spread are separate from that organ-level definition.

sentences.text: It is a gland in the male reproductive system that contributes fluid to semen. A prostate cancer study’s stage and spread are separate from that organ-level definition.

guides.scope: Itraconazole research in advanced prostate cancer, with separate PSA and disease-progression outcomes.

guides.title: Non-small-cell lung cancer
guides.description: Itraconazole added to pemetrexed in a small trial of advanced nonsquamous lung cancer.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Non-small cell lung cancer includes several types, particularly adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. The pemetrexed–itraconazole trial enrolled the nonsquamous subgroup with metastatic disease.

sentences.text: Non-small cell lung cancer includes several types, particularly adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. The pemetrexed–itraconazole trial enrolled the nonsquamous subgroup with metastatic disease.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Adding itraconazole to pemetrexed produced encouraging survival estimates in a trial that enrolled only 23 people before stopping early. The small sample makes those estimates uncertain.

sentences.text: Adding itraconazole to pemetrexed produced encouraging survival estimates in a trial that enrolled only 23 people before stopping early. The small sample makes those estimates uncertain.

questions.question: What happened to progression-free survival?
questions.answer: Median progression-free survival was 5.5 months with the combination and 2.8 months with pemetrexed alone; the difference did not reach conventional statistical significance (P=0.089).

sentences.text: Median progression-free survival was 5.5 months with the combination and 2.8 months with pemetrexed alone; the difference did not reach conventional statistical significance (P=0.089).

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: The study’s small enrollment limits detection of uncommon harms from adding itraconazole to chemotherapy.

sentences.text: The study’s small enrollment limits detection of uncommon harms from adding itraconazole to chemotherapy.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Median overall survival was 32 versus 8 months, but this was a small, prematurely closed phase II study. It did not compare the combination with modern molecularly targeted or immunotherapy regimens.

sentences.text: Median overall survival was 32 versus 8 months, but this was a small, prematurely closed phase II study. It did not compare the combination with modern molecularly targeted or immunotherapy regimens.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Early closure followed changing use of pemetrexed in lung-cancer care. With only 23 participants, the trial was too small for stable efficacy estimates.

sentences.text: Early closure followed changing use of pemetrexed in lung-cancer care. With only 23 participants, the trial was too small for stable efficacy estimates.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The itraconazole profile compares its antifungal action with cancer-related angiogenesis and Hedgehog hypotheses.

sentences.text: The itraconazole profile compares its antifungal action with cancer-related angiogenesis and Hedgehog hypotheses.

faqs.question: Is nonsquamous disease the whole NSCLC category?
faqs.answer: No. Non-small cell lung cancer includes squamous and nonsquamous types. The itraconazole–pemetrexed study selected nonsquamous disease.

sentences.text: No. Non-small cell lung cancer includes squamous and nonsquamous types. The itraconazole–pemetrexed study selected nonsquamous disease.

guides.scope: Itraconazole added to pemetrexed in a small trial of advanced nonsquamous lung cancer.

guides.title: Breast cancer
guides.description: Metformin’s metabolic rationale and the negative disease-free-survival result of the MA.32 breast-cancer trial.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Breast cancer arises in breast tissue and includes tumors with different hormone-receptor and HER2 characteristics. Repurposing research has asked whether changing insulin and metabolism can improve outcomes alongside standard cancer care.

sentences.text: Breast cancer arises in breast tissue and includes tumors with different hormone-receptor and HER2 characteristics. Repurposing research has asked whether changing insulin and metabolism can improve outcomes alongside standard cancer care.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: The large MA.32 trial did not show an invasive disease-free-survival benefit from adding metformin to standard therapy in people without diabetes who had high-risk, operable breast cancer.

sentences.text: The large MA.32 trial did not show an invasive disease-free-survival benefit from adding metformin to standard therapy in people without diabetes who had high-risk, operable breast cancer.

questions.question: Did metabolic changes translate into better cancer outcomes?
questions.answer: Metformin affected metabolic measures, including insulin-related factors, but the phase III cancer-outcome trial did not establish the hoped-for benefit.

sentences.text: Metformin affected metabolic measures, including insulin-related factors, but the phase III cancer-outcome trial did not establish the hoped-for benefit.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: MA.32 evaluated prolonged metformin exposure in people without diabetes. Metformin’s renal restrictions and gastrointestinal adverse effects remain relevant when considering prolonged additional treatment.

sentences.text: MA.32 evaluated prolonged metformin exposure in people without diabetes. Metformin’s renal restrictions and gastrointestinal adverse effects remain relevant when considering prolonged additional treatment.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: MA.32 compared metformin with placebo on top of standard breast-cancer treatment. Its findings do not answer whether treating diabetes with metformin should be changed in someone who also has breast cancer.

sentences.text: MA.32 compared metformin with placebo on top of standard breast-cancer treatment. Its findings do not answer whether treating diabetes with metformin should be changed in someone who also has breast cancer.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: MA.32 enrolled 3,649 participants and tested metformin over a planned five-year treatment period. Its randomized clinical endpoint is more directly informative about recurrence than earlier metabolic associations.

sentences.text: MA.32 enrolled 3,649 participants and tested metformin over a planned five-year treatment period. Its randomized clinical endpoint is more directly informative about recurrence than earlier metabolic associations.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The pancreatic cancer page describes a separate negative metformin trial in advanced disease; the two results should retain their different populations.

sentences.text: The pancreatic cancer page describes a separate negative metformin trial in advanced disease; the two results should retain their different populations.

faqs.question: Does a breast-cancer diagnosis identify one tumor biology?
faqs.answer: No. Hormone receptors and HER2 status distinguish clinically important tumor groups. Findings need to be read in the population actually enrolled.

sentences.text: No. Hormone receptors and HER2 status distinguish clinically important tumor groups. Findings need to be read in the population actually enrolled.

guides.scope: Metformin’s metabolic rationale and the negative disease-free-survival result of the MA.32 breast-cancer trial.

guides.title: Colorectal cancer
guides.description: Aspirin after surgery for colorectal cancers with selected PI3K-pathway alterations.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Colorectal cancer begins in the colon or rectum. ALASCCA studied whether aspirin could reduce recurrence after surgery in localized cancers with selected PI3K-pathway gene alterations.

sentences.text: Colorectal cancer begins in the colon or rectum. ALASCCA studied whether aspirin could reduce recurrence after surgery in localized cancers with selected PI3K-pathway gene alterations.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: ALASCCA found fewer recurrences with aspirin in its molecularly selected population. This result applies to the tested postoperative setting and gene alterations, rather than to every colorectal cancer.

sentences.text: ALASCCA found fewer recurrences with aspirin in its molecularly selected population. This result applies to the tested postoperative setting and gene alterations, rather than to every colorectal cancer.

questions.question: How large was the recurrence difference?
questions.answer: For tumors with the prespecified PIK3CA hotspot mutations, estimated three-year recurrence was 7.7% with aspirin versus 14.1% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.49; 95% CI 0.24–0.98).

sentences.text: For tumors with the prespecified PIK3CA hotspot mutations, estimated three-year recurrence was 7.7% with aspirin versus 14.1% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.49; 95% CI 0.24–0.98).

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Severe adverse events occurred in 16.8% of the aspirin group and 11.6% of the placebo group. The benefit therefore needs to be considered alongside harm, even with a familiar medicine.

sentences.text: Severe adverse events occurred in 16.8% of the aspirin group and 11.6% of the placebo group. The benefit therefore needs to be considered alongside harm, even with a familiar medicine.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: The comparison was aspirin versus placebo after cancer treatment. It was not aspirin instead of surgery or indicated chemotherapy.

sentences.text: The comparison was aspirin versus placebo after cancer treatment. It was not aspirin instead of surgery or indicated chemotherapy.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: ALASCCA used tumor PI3K-pathway alterations to define two molecular groups and followed recurrence for three years. Molecular eligibility is essential to applying its result.

sentences.text: ALASCCA used tumor PI3K-pathway alterations to define two molecular groups and followed recurrence for three years. Molecular eligibility is essential to applying its result.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The aspirin profile covers its established platelet action; the liver-cancer page addresses an observational prevention question rather than postoperative recurrence.

sentences.text: The aspirin profile covers its established platelet action; the liver-cancer page addresses an observational prevention question rather than postoperative recurrence.

faqs.question: Why does the location of colorectal cancer matter?
faqs.answer: Colon and rectal cancers share a broad category but can require different local treatment approaches. ALASCCA specified eligible stages separately for colon and rectal tumors.

sentences.text: Colon and rectal cancers share a broad category but can require different local treatment approaches. ALASCCA specified eligible stages separately for colon and rectal tumors.

guides.scope: Aspirin after surgery for colorectal cancers with selected PI3K-pathway alterations.

guides.title: Pancreatic cancer
guides.description: Why metformin was tested in advanced pancreatic cancer and why the randomized result was negative.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Pancreatic cancer begins in the pancreas; the metformin trial studied advanced disease. Its purpose was to add a metabolic intervention to gemcitabine and erlotinib.

sentences.text: Pancreatic cancer begins in the pancreas; the metformin trial studied advanced disease. Its purpose was to add a metabolic intervention to gemcitabine and erlotinib.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: In a randomized trial of 121 people, adding metformin did not improve survival over placebo with the same anticancer regimen.

sentences.text: In a randomized trial of 121 people, adding metformin did not improve survival over placebo with the same anticancer regimen.

questions.question: Was metformin used as a replacement for chemotherapy?
questions.answer: No. Both groups received gemcitabine and erlotinib. The study tested the extra effect of metformin, which was not beneficial for survival in this setting.

sentences.text: No. Both groups received gemcitabine and erlotinib. The study tested the extra effect of metformin, which was not beneficial for survival in this setting.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Grade 3–4 diarrhea and fatigue were each reported in 10% with metformin, versus 5% and 3% with placebo; severe neutropenia occurred in 25% in each group.

sentences.text: Grade 3–4 diarrhea and fatigue were each reported in 10% with metformin, versus 5% and 3% with placebo; severe neutropenia occurred in 25% in each group.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: This result concerns metformin added to a specific advanced-cancer regimen. It does not test pancreatic-cancer prevention or treatment of diabetes itself.

sentences.text: This result concerns metformin added to a specific advanced-cancer regimen. It does not test pancreatic-cancer prevention or treatment of diabetes itself.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The phase II trial used random assignment and blinding, with identical background anticancer treatment. This design directly tests the incremental survival effect of metformin.

sentences.text: The phase II trial used random assignment and blinding, with identical background anticancer treatment. This design directly tests the incremental survival effect of metformin.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The breast cancer page describes metformin after treatment of operable cancer, a distinct setting from the advanced pancreatic trial.

sentences.text: The breast cancer page describes metformin after treatment of operable cancer, a distinct setting from the advanced pancreatic trial.

faqs.question: Did the metformin trial study localized operable cancer?
faqs.answer: No. It studied advanced pancreatic cancer; it does not supply a postoperative recurrence estimate.

sentences.text: No. It studied advanced pancreatic cancer; it does not supply a postoperative recurrence estimate.

guides.scope: Why metformin was tested in advanced pancreatic cancer and why the randomized result was negative.

guides.title: Melanoma
guides.description: Propranolol as an experimental addition to immune checkpoint treatment in melanoma.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Melanoma develops from pigment-producing melanocytes. In advanced disease, immune checkpoint drugs and, for eligible tumors, molecularly targeted treatments are important treatment approaches.

sentences.text: Melanoma develops from pigment-producing melanocytes. In advanced disease, immune checkpoint drugs and, for eligible tumors, molecularly targeted treatments are important treatment approaches.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: A nine-person phase I study explored propranolol with pembrolizumab in advanced melanoma. It demonstrated feasibility and observed tumor responses, but had no pembrolizumab-only group to establish added benefit.

sentences.text: A nine-person phase I study explored propranolol with pembrolizumab in advanced melanoma. It demonstrated feasibility and observed tumor responses, but had no pembrolizumab-only group to establish added benefit.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the propranolol trial?
questions.answer: The study primarily assessed safety and tolerability of combining beta-blockade with pembrolizumab. Tumor response was an early activity signal.

sentences.text: The study primarily assessed safety and tolerability of combining beta-blockade with pembrolizumab. Tumor response was an early activity signal.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: No dose-limiting toxicity was identified in this small study. Rash, fatigue and vitiligo were each reported in four of the nine participants.

sentences.text: No dose-limiting toxicity was identified in this small study. Rash, fatigue and vitiligo were each reported in four of the nine participants.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: The trial cannot determine whether propranolol improves pembrolizumab’s response rate or survival benefit, because all participants received the combination.

sentences.text: The trial cannot determine whether propranolol improves pembrolizumab’s response rate or survival benefit, because all participants received the combination.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Nine participants are enough for an initial combination-safety exploration, but not for a dependable comparison of response or survival against pembrolizumab alone.

sentences.text: Nine participants are enough for an initial combination-safety exploration, but not for a dependable comparison of response or survival against pembrolizumab alone.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The propranolol profile explains beta-blockade; the basal cell carcinoma page covers a different skin cancer and a different repurposing target.

sentences.text: The propranolol profile explains beta-blockade; the basal cell carcinoma page covers a different skin cancer and a different repurposing target.

faqs.question: Why is a melanoma mutation result relevant to treatment?
faqs.answer: Some melanoma treatments target altered tumor pathways, including BRAF. Eligibility for those therapies is a different question from propranolol’s proposed effect on the immune environment.

sentences.text: Some melanoma treatments target altered tumor pathways, including BRAF. Eligibility for those therapies is a different question from propranolol’s proposed effect on the immune environment.

guides.scope: Propranolol as an experimental addition to immune checkpoint treatment in melanoma.

guides.title: Basal-cell carcinoma
guides.description: Itraconazole’s Hedgehog-pathway activity and early tumor changes in basal cell carcinoma.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Basal cell carcinoma begins in basal cells in the lower epidermis. It usually grows slowly but can invade surrounding tissue. Itraconazole has been studied because Hedgehog signaling is important in this cancer.

sentences.text: Basal cell carcinoma begins in basal cells in the lower epidermis. It usually grows slowly but can invade surrounding tissue. Itraconazole has been studied because Hedgehog signaling is important in this cancer.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: In an exploratory study, itraconazole reduced tumor area and markers of tumor-cell proliferation. These short-term changes do not establish durable cure or recurrence prevention.

sentences.text: In an exploratory study, itraconazole reduced tumor area and markers of tumor-cell proliferation. These short-term changes do not establish durable cure or recurrence prevention.

questions.question: How much did tumor area change?
questions.answer: Among the treated study participants, mean tumor area fell by 24% (95% CI 18.2–30.0%). The study was small and open-label.

sentences.text: Among the treated study participants, mean tumor area fell by 24% (95% CI 18.2–30.0%). The study was small and open-label.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Adverse events included moderate fatigue and a grade 4 congestive-heart-failure event, an important concern despite the small study size.

sentences.text: Adverse events included moderate fatigue and a grade 4 congestive-heart-failure event, an important concern despite the small study size.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: This study does not compare itraconazole with curative local treatment or with approved Hedgehog-pathway drugs.

sentences.text: This study does not compare itraconazole with curative local treatment or with approved Hedgehog-pathway drugs.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Nineteen of 29 enrolled participants received itraconazole. The study measured tumor proliferation, signaling and area, not a definitive long-term cure endpoint.

sentences.text: Nineteen of 29 enrolled participants received itraconazole. The study measured tumor proliferation, signaling and area, not a definitive long-term cure endpoint.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The melanoma page makes clear why evidence from one skin cancer cannot be assigned to another.

sentences.text: The melanoma page makes clear why evidence from one skin cancer cannot be assigned to another.

faqs.question: Is basal cell carcinoma the same as melanoma?
faqs.answer: No. Basal cell carcinoma arises from basal cells, while melanoma develops from melanocytes. Their biology and treatment evidence are different.

sentences.text: No. Basal cell carcinoma arises from basal cells, while melanoma develops from melanocytes. Their biology and treatment evidence are different.

guides.scope: Itraconazole’s Hedgehog-pathway activity and early tumor changes in basal cell carcinoma.

guides.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma
guides.description: Aspirin research on liver-cancer risk in chronic viral hepatitis, distinct from treatment of established cancer.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Hepatocellular carcinoma is the most common primary liver cancer and begins in hepatocytes. Chronic hepatitis B or C infection and cirrhosis are important risk contexts.

sentences.text: Hepatocellular carcinoma is the most common primary liver cancer and begins in hepatocytes. Chronic hepatitis B or C infection and cirrhosis are important risk contexts.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: A Swedish observational study associated aspirin use with lower subsequent liver-cancer incidence among people with chronic viral hepatitis. This was prevention research, not a trial treating existing hepatocellular carcinoma.

sentences.text: A Swedish observational study associated aspirin use with lower subsequent liver-cancer incidence among people with chronic viral hepatitis. This was prevention research, not a trial treating existing hepatocellular carcinoma.

questions.question: What difference was observed?
questions.answer: Ten-year estimated cancer incidence was 4.0% among aspirin users and 8.3% among nonusers; the adjusted hazard ratio was 0.69 (95% CI 0.62–0.76).

sentences.text: Ten-year estimated cancer incidence was 4.0% among aspirin users and 8.3% among nonusers; the adjusted hazard ratio was 0.69 (95% CI 0.62–0.76).

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: The investigators also examined bleeding outcomes. Decisions in people with chronic liver disease must account for bleeding susceptibility alongside any proposed preventive benefit.

sentences.text: The investigators also examined bleeding outcomes. Decisions in people with chronic liver disease must account for bleeding susceptibility alongside any proposed preventive benefit.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: A lower incidence of future cancer cannot be treated as evidence that aspirin shrinks an established liver tumor or improves survival after a cancer diagnosis.

sentences.text: A lower incidence of future cancer cannot be treated as evidence that aspirin shrinks an established liver tumor or improves survival after a cancer diagnosis.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The cohort analysis adjusted for measured differences between aspirin users and nonusers. Unmeasured differences can remain, and the cancer-incidence association is not a randomized treatment effect.

sentences.text: The cohort analysis adjusted for measured differences between aspirin users and nonusers. Unmeasured differences can remain, and the cancer-incidence association is not a randomized treatment effect.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The colorectal cancer page discusses a randomized aspirin study after surgery, contrasting with the prevention association in viral hepatitis.

sentences.text: The colorectal cancer page discusses a randomized aspirin study after surgery, contrasting with the prevention association in viral hepatitis.

faqs.question: Is every cancer found in the liver hepatocellular carcinoma?
faqs.answer: No. Hepatocellular carcinoma begins in the liver’s hepatocytes. Cancers that spread to the liver from another organ are a different disease category.

sentences.text: No. Hepatocellular carcinoma begins in the liver’s hepatocytes. Cancers that spread to the liver from another organ are a different disease category.

guides.scope: Aspirin research on liver-cancer risk in chronic viral hepatitis, distinct from treatment of established cancer.

guides.title: Multiple myeloma
guides.description: Thalidomide’s transition to an established myeloma treatment and its distinctive safety risks.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow. It can damage bone and interfere with healthy blood-cell production. Thalidomide is an example of repurposing that reached an approved cancer indication.

sentences.text: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow. It can damage bone and interfere with healthy blood-cell production. Thalidomide is an example of repurposing that reached an approved cancer indication.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Thalidomide with dexamethasone is FDA-approved for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma. Its status differs from exploratory repurposing candidates supported only by laboratory or small early clinical studies.

sentences.text: Thalidomide with dexamethasone is FDA-approved for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma. Its status differs from exploratory repurposing candidates supported only by laboratory or small early clinical studies.

questions.question: Is thalidomide an investigational myeloma treatment?
questions.answer: Its combination with dexamethasone has an established approved indication. The appropriate regimen still depends on the patient’s disease and treatment context.

sentences.text: Its combination with dexamethasone has an established approved indication. The appropriate regimen still depends on the patient’s disease and treatment context.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Thalidomide can cause severe birth defects and blood clots. Nerve damage is another clinically important risk of this drug class; these hazards are integral to treatment selection and monitoring.

sentences.text: Thalidomide can cause severe birth defects and blood clots. Nerve damage is another clinically important risk of this drug class; these hazards are integral to treatment selection and monitoring.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Thalidomide belongs to the same broad immunomodulatory treatment family as lenalidomide and pomalidomide. They are distinct medicines and are not interchangeable solely because they share that category.

sentences.text: Thalidomide belongs to the same broad immunomodulatory treatment family as lenalidomide and pomalidomide. They are distinct medicines and are not interchangeable solely because they share that category.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: FDA approval of thalidomide with dexamethasone represents an established myeloma indication. The relevant evidence question is the benefit and harm of the particular combination and treatment setting.

sentences.text: FDA approval of thalidomide with dexamethasone represents an established myeloma indication. The relevant evidence question is the benefit and harm of the particular combination and treatment setting.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The thalidomide profile follows the repurposing history, approved combination and distinctive immune effects.

sentences.text: The thalidomide profile follows the repurposing history, approved combination and distinctive immune effects.

faqs.question: Why can myeloma cause bone and blood problems?
faqs.answer: Abnormal plasma cells accumulate in bone marrow, interfering with normal blood-cell production and contributing to bone damage.

sentences.text: Abnormal plasma cells accumulate in bone marrow, interfering with normal blood-cell production and contributing to bone damage.

guides.scope: Thalidomide’s transition to an established myeloma treatment and its distinctive safety risks.

guides.title: Acute myeloid leukemia
guides.description: Valproate as an addition to decitabine in older adults with acute myeloid leukemia.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Acute myeloid leukemia is a fast-growing cancer of blood-forming cells in the bone marrow. Repurposing studies have explored medicines that alter the gene regulation of leukemia cells.

sentences.text: Acute myeloid leukemia is a fast-growing cancer of blood-forming cells in the bone marrow. Repurposing studies have explored medicines that alter the gene regulation of leukemia cells.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: In older adults unsuitable for intensive chemotherapy, a randomized trial did not find a survival advantage from adding valproate to decitabine.

sentences.text: In older adults unsuitable for intensive chemotherapy, a randomized trial did not find a survival advantage from adding valproate to decitabine.

questions.question: Was the favorable result in this trial due to valproate?
questions.answer: No. The factorial trial tested valproate and all-trans retinoic acid separately. Favorable remission and survival findings were associated with the retinoic-acid assignment, not valproate.

sentences.text: No. The factorial trial tested valproate and all-trans retinoic acid separately. Favorable remission and survival findings were associated with the retinoic-acid assignment, not valproate.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: The population consisted of older people ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. Tolerability and competing illness in this group are part of the clinical context, and the lack of a survival benefit does not justify adding treatment burden.

sentences.text: The population consisted of older people ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. Tolerability and competing illness in this group are part of the clinical context, and the lack of a survival benefit does not justify adding treatment burden.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: The factorial design separates the valproate question from the retinoic-acid question. It should not be summarized as though every drug in the combination produced the same result.

sentences.text: The factorial design separates the valproate question from the retinoic-acid question. It should not be summarized as though every drug in the combination produced the same result.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The factorial design independently allocated the added medicines, allowing the valproate and retinoic-acid effects to be separated. A favorable result for one cannot be assigned to both.

sentences.text: The factorial design independently allocated the added medicines, allowing the valproate and retinoic-acid effects to be separated. A favorable result for one cannot be assigned to both.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The valproic acid profile and head and neck cancer page examine epigenetic combinations with different treatments and toxicity findings.

sentences.text: The valproic acid profile and head and neck cancer page examine epigenetic combinations with different treatments and toxicity findings.

faqs.question: Why is AML described as acute?
faqs.answer: The abnormal immature blood cells increase rapidly and impair normal blood formation. That rapid course distinguishes it from slower chronic leukemias.

sentences.text: The abnormal immature blood cells increase rapidly and impair normal blood formation. That rapid course distinguishes it from slower chronic leukemias.

guides.scope: Valproate as an addition to decitabine in older adults with acute myeloid leukemia.

guides.title: Chronic myeloid leukemia
guides.description: Pioglitazone research aimed at deeper molecular responses in chronic myeloid leukemia.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Chronic myeloid leukemia involves abnormal myeloid blood cells. Pioglitazone has been studied alongside imatinib to target persistent leukemia cells after an initial molecular response.

sentences.text: Chronic myeloid leukemia involves abnormal myeloid blood cells. Pioglitazone has been studied alongside imatinib to target persistent leukemia cells after an initial molecular response.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: The ACTIM study reported deep molecular responses after adding pioglitazone to imatinib. Its single-arm design cannot establish how many responses were caused by pioglitazone rather than continued imatinib treatment.

sentences.text: The ACTIM study reported deep molecular responses after adding pioglitazone to imatinib. Its single-arm design cannot establish how many responses were caused by pioglitazone rather than continued imatinib treatment.

questions.question: Was pioglitazone tested instead of imatinib?
questions.answer: No. Participants continued imatinib, and the question was whether adding pioglitazone could deepen an existing molecular response.

sentences.text: No. Participants continued imatinib, and the question was whether adding pioglitazone could deepen an existing molecular response.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Edema led one ACTIM participant to stop pioglitazone. Fluid retention is especially relevant when adding this medicine to an ongoing cancer regimen.

sentences.text: Edema led one ACTIM participant to stop pioglitazone. Fluid retention is especially relevant when adding this medicine to an ongoing cancer regimen.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: ACTIM did not include a randomized imatinib-only group. Historical response rates offer context but cannot provide an equally reliable treatment comparison.

sentences.text: ACTIM did not include a randomized imatinib-only group. Historical response rates offer context but cannot provide an equally reliable treatment comparison.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: ACTIM used a molecular endpoint, MR4.5, indicating very low BCR::ABL1 transcript levels. The absence of concurrent randomization limits attribution of deeper response.

sentences.text: ACTIM used a molecular endpoint, MR4.5, indicating very low BCR::ABL1 transcript levels. The absence of concurrent randomization limits attribution of deeper response.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The pioglitazone profile describes PPARγ activation, the mechanism proposed to complement imatinib.

sentences.text: The pioglitazone profile describes PPARγ activation, the mechanism proposed to complement imatinib.

faqs.question: What is measured in a CML molecular response?
faqs.answer: The test measures BCR::ABL1 transcripts. MR4.5 indicates a very deep reduction, and is different from an ordinary blood count becoming normal.

sentences.text: The test measures BCR::ABL1 transcripts. MR4.5 indicates a very deep reduction, and is different from an ordinary blood count becoming normal.

guides.scope: Pioglitazone research aimed at deeper molecular responses in chronic myeloid leukemia.

guides.title: Parkinson disease
guides.description: Metformin’s neuroprotective rationale and the clinical results of a small Parkinson’s pilot.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Parkinson’s disease affects movement and many nonmotor functions. Loss of dopamine-producing neurons contributes to slowness, stiffness and tremor; levodopa helps movement symptoms but does not replace lost neurons.

sentences.text: Parkinson’s disease affects movement and many nonmotor functions. Loss of dopamine-producing neurons contributes to slowness, stiffness and tremor; levodopa helps movement symptoms but does not replace lost neurons.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: A metformin pilot in people already taking levodopa/carbidopa did not demonstrate better clinical scores than placebo after three months. This matters because improvement within the metformin group alone can overstate the treatment effect.

sentences.text: A metformin pilot in people already taking levodopa/carbidopa did not demonstrate better clinical scores than placebo after three months. This matters because improvement within the metformin group alone can overstate the treatment effect.

questions.question: Did metformin improve the main Parkinson’s score?
questions.answer: The post-treatment between-group comparison for total UPDRS was not significant (P=0.515). Clinical subscores also did not show significant between-group differences.

sections.label: Safety

sentences.text: Schizophrenia can involve psychotic symptoms, reduced motivation and expression, and cognitive difficulties such as problems with attention or working memory. These symptom domains require different outcome measures.

sentences.text: Multiple sclerosis damages myelin and nerve fibers in the central nervous system. A clinically isolated syndrome is a first neurological episode suggestive of inflammatory demyelination; it is a specific early setting for treatment research.

sentences.text: Vitiligo causes loss of pigment when melanocytes are destroyed or stop functioning. Autoimmune processes are important in the disease, and visible skin changes can substantially affect quality of life.

sentences.text: Sarcopenia involves declining muscle strength and function, often with reduced muscle mass. Difficulty rising from a chair, slower walking and increased falls can threaten independence. Resistance activity and adequate nutrition are central to preserving muscle health.

sections.label: Options

guides.title: Drug repurposing
guides.description: How existing medicines become candidates for new uses, and how mechanisms, clinical evidence and approval fit together.
guides.scope: How existing medicines become candidates for new uses, and how mechanisms, clinical evidence and approval fit together.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: Overview
sections.paragraph: Drug repurposing investigates whether an existing medicine or investigational compound can treat a different condition. The starting point is prior knowledge about the compound; the new use remains a question to test.

sentences.text: Drug repurposing investigates whether an existing medicine or investigational compound can treat a different condition.
The starting point is prior knowledge about the compound; the new use remains a question to test.

sections.label: Rationale
sections.title: Why repurpose a drug?
sections.paragraph: Existing compounds may already have manufacturing, laboratory and human data, allowing researchers to build on earlier development. That can shorten some development steps, although a new indication still needs evidence and may face funding barriers, especially for off-patent medicines.

sentences.text: Existing compounds may already have manufacturing, laboratory and human data, allowing researchers to build on earlier development.
That can shorten some development steps, although a new indication still needs evidence and may face funding barriers, especially for off-patent medicines.

sections.label: Mechanisms
sections.title: Mechanisms
sections.paragraph: A mechanism of action describes the biological steps through which a drug acts. Researchers can look for a relevant target or disease process, screen compounds, and confirm activity in cells or animals before clinical testing. Examples of biological questions include effects on the Hedgehog pathway, apoptosis, autophagy or angiogenesis. Each names a process to investigate, not a promise that changing it will improve a disease.

sentences.text: A mechanism of action describes the biological steps through which a drug acts. Researchers can look for a relevant target or disease process, screen compounds, and confirm activity in cells or animals before clinical testing.

Examples of biological questions include effects on the Hedgehog pathway, apoptosis, autophagy or angiogenesis. Each names a process to investigate, not a promise that changing it will improve a disease.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.title: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Basic research tests biological ideas; translational research develops them toward possible interventions; clinical trials evaluate effects in people. Controlled trials compare a treatment group with standard care or an inactive control, helping distinguish treatment effects from what would otherwise happen. For a repurposing claim, read the population, treatment, comparison and measured outcome together. A laboratory pathway change answers a different question from improved symptoms or survival.

sentences.text: Basic research tests biological ideas; translational research develops them toward possible interventions; clinical trials evaluate effects in people.
Controlled trials compare a treatment group with standard care or an inactive control, helping distinguish treatment effects from what would otherwise happen.
For a repurposing claim, read the population, treatment, comparison and measured outcome together. A laboratory pathway change answers a different question from improved symptoms or survival.

sections.label: Status
sections.title: Approval and off-label use
sections.paragraph: Off-label use means prescribing an approved drug outside its approved indication, route or dose. In the United States, clinicians may do this when medically appropriate, but FDA has not determined safety and effectiveness for that unapproved use. Repurposing is the research and development question; off-label use is a prescribing status. A successful repurposing program can seek a new approved indication.

sentences.text: Off-label use means prescribing an approved drug outside its approved indication, route or dose. In the United States, clinicians may do this when medically appropriate, but FDA has not determined safety and effectiveness for that unapproved use.
Repurposing is the research and development question; off-label use is a prescribing status. A successful repurposing program can seek a new approved indication.

sections.label: Safety
sections.title: Safety
sections.paragraph: Approval for one use does not mean a medicine is free of risks. The intended condition, dose and route matter when weighing benefits and harms. Metformin’s established role in type 2 diabetes, for example, does not remove its kidney-related restrictions or lactic-acidosis warning.

sentences.text: Approval for one use does not mean a medicine is free of risks. The intended condition, dose and route matter when weighing benefits and harms.
Metformin’s established role in type 2 diabetes, for example, does not remove its kidney-related restrictions or lactic-acidosis warning.

sections.label: Reading
sections.title: Reading a repurposing claim
sections.paragraph: Ask what the medicine is already approved for, what studies support the proposed use, how it compares with available treatments, and what harms are possible. Then examine study design and outcomes: an experimental result is most useful when the comparison and the question it answers are clear.

sentences.text: Ask what the medicine is already approved for, what studies support the proposed use, how it compares with available treatments, and what harms are possible.
Then examine study design and outcomes: an experimental result is most useful when the comparison and the question it answers are clear.

faqs.question: Does an approved medicine already have evidence for every new use?
faqs.answer: No. FDA approval concerns specified uses; a different indication needs its own assessment of safety and effectiveness.

sentences.text: No. FDA approval concerns specified uses; a different indication needs its own assessment of safety and effectiveness.

faqs.question: Why include mechanisms when clinical outcomes matter?
faqs.answer: Mechanisms help formulate and test a rationale. Clinical studies then assess whether that rationale translates into useful effects in people.

sentences.text: Mechanisms help formulate and test a rationale. Clinical studies then assess whether that rationale translates into useful effects in people.

guides.title: Type 2 diabetes

guides.scope: Insulin resistance, blood glucose and the established role of metformin, with links to the wider drug-repurposing evidence.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Type 2 diabetes is a condition in which blood glucose remains too high because tissues do not respond adequately to insulin and the pancreas cannot supply enough insulin to compensate. Over time, diabetes can damage the eyes, kidneys, nerves and cardiovascular system.

sentences.text: Type 2 diabetes is a condition in which blood glucose remains too high because tissues do not respond adequately to insulin and the pancreas cannot supply enough insulin to compensate.
Over time, diabetes can damage the eyes, kidneys, nerves and cardiovascular system.

sections.label: Options

sentences.text: Management combines healthy daily habits, monitoring and medicines selected for the person’s glucose levels and other health conditions.
Metformin is an established glucose-lowering treatment for type 2 diabetes, rather than an experimental repurposing use in this condition.

questions.question: What is metformin’s role here?
questions.answer: Metformin is labeled as an addition to diet and exercise to improve blood glucose control in type 2 diabetes.

sentences.text: Metformin is labeled as an addition to diet and exercise to improve blood glucose control in type 2 diabetes.

questions.question: Why do people with type 2 diabetes receive different medicines?

sentences.text: Treatment choices depend on glucose control, other illnesses, medicine costs and access, as well as the person’s circumstances.

sections.label: Evidence

sentences.text: Glucose control, blood pressure and cholesterol management contribute to reducing diabetes-related health risks.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Monitoring helps identify glucose levels that are too high or too low, particularly when medicines are used. Metformin has a lactic-acidosis warning and is contraindicated in severe renal impairment.

sentences.text: Monitoring helps identify glucose levels that are too high or too low, particularly when medicines are used.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Type 1 diabetes involves immune destruction of insulin-producing cells. Type 2 diabetes involves ineffective insulin action together with an insulin supply that cannot meet the body’s needs. Prediabetes describes elevated glucose below the diagnostic range for diabetes; it is a different stage, not another name for established type 2 diabetes.

sentences.text: Type 1 diabetes involves immune destruction of insulin-producing cells. Type 2 diabetes involves ineffective insulin action together with an insulin supply that cannot meet the body’s needs.
Prediabetes describes elevated glucose below the diagnostic range for diabetes; it is a different stage, not another name for established type 2 diabetes.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: Metformin’s glucose-lowering action provides an established-use reference when reading its drug-repurposing research. An effect on glucose control should be distinguished from a finding about a different disease or clinical outcome.

sentences.text: Metformin’s glucose-lowering action provides an established-use reference when reading its drug-repurposing research.
An effect on glucose control should be distinguished from a finding about a different disease or clinical outcome.

sections.paragraph: Fluconazole is a triazole antifungal medicine used for susceptible fungal infections, including Candida infections and fungal meningitis. It slows fungal growth; its established infection uses do not establish benefit for unrelated diseases.
